title: Region choice onboarding visual deck and compact map cards
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Purpose: Produce a small, flexible visual asset set that explains region and latency routing behavior for the Redwood Console quickstart and docs. Goal is to clarify how routing decisions are made, what customers can expect from the ‘region preference’ control, and how fallback/degenerate cases look in the UI. Deliverables listed below include static hero artwork for the quickstart page, compact map + card components for in-console tooltips, a micro-interactive prototype for the docs page, and annotated screenshot overlays for release notes.

Why this matters: New customers often ask whether Redwood will route requests to nearest GPU region, and how latency vs cost tradeoffs are handled. Current docs lean on prose and a single map image; we need concise visuals that reduce support queries and make rollout options discoverable during onboarding.

Deliverables (final assets):
- Hero static illustration (SVG + PNG) showing three routing scenarios: preferred-region hit, cross-region fallback, and multi-variant fallback (cheapest vs lowest-latency).
- Compact region-card component pack (3 sizes: xs/s/m) for console route list and callout tooltips (SVG, PNG, CSS tokens).
- Interactive micro-map prototype (Figma prototype with hover states and a simulated request timeline).
- Annotated screenshot overlays for release notes and the console tour (PNG with labeled callouts).
- Accessibility spec sheet: color contrast values, alt-text copy, keyboard-only interaction notes.

Design decisions and constraints:
- Visual language should match Console UI (tokens in /design-system/token-2026). Use existing accent palette (blue-600 for primary region), red-500 for degraded/fallback flows, and neutral-600 for background lines.
- Map art will be simplified geographical outlines with node icons representing regions (no live map tiles). Keep icons geometric for clarity at small sizes.
- Compact card must render clearly at 240x140 (xs), 320x220 (s), and 480x320 (m). Provide 2x PNGs for HiDPI. Provide SVGs with viewBox sizing and separate path outlines for easier engineering stroke control.
- Interactions: hover shows latency and last-seen timestamp; clicking opens the route details panel. Prototype will show three-step timeline for a single request (client -> nearest region -> fallback if saturated -> final response).

Open trade-offs:
- Real map tiles would be more realistic but increase weight and licensing work; for onboarding we prefer lightweight vector art to keep docs performant.
- Showing live latency numbers risks implying guarantees; UI language must include “typical latency shown” disclaimer. Work with PM copy to finalize microcopy.

Acceptance criteria:
- Assets exported (SVG + PNG @1x/2x) uploaded to gs://redwood-design-assets/region-routing/2026-03- and referenced in the Console quickstart and docs.
- Figma prototype link shared and embedded in docs.
- Engineering receives a single assets ZIP with responsive specs and an integration checklist (CSS classes, token names, breakpoints).
- Accessibility checklist completed and reviewed by Accessibility reviewer.

Integration notes for Engineering:
- Provide final SVGs with separate groups for node icons, path strokes, and labels. Engineers asked for 8px and 12px grid snaps and CSS variables for colors.
- Provide token mapping to Console token names: --rwd-color-primary: blue-600; --rwd-color-fallback: amber-500; --rwd-stroke-muted: neutral-300.

Where work lives (links):
- Figma file: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/region-routing-onboarding-2026
- Prototype: https://www.figma.com/proto/abcd1234/region-routing-proto
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Design/Region+Routing+Visuals
- Asset bucket (export target): gs://redwood-design-assets/region-routing/2026-03/
